name: Nimesulide
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) restricted in Europe since 2007 and 2012 (second-line, acute pain or primary dysmenorrhea only, maximum 15 days) because of liver injury. About half a dose is excreted in urine; in mild to moderate kidney impairment exposure rises about 50% without accumulation. The European harmonized text needs no change at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 30–80 mL/min and contraindicates it below 30 mL/min. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European harmonized summary of product characteristics (EMA 2004; kidney thresholds unchanged by the 2007 and 2012 reviews) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min). Indications and duration follow EMA 2012.

bands.recommendation: Usual: 100 mg twice daily after meals, maximum 15 days; second-line for acute pain or primary dysmenorrhea only (EMA 2012).
CrCl 30–80: no dose adjustment (EMA 2004). Caution: kidney function may deteriorate; stop if it does.

crrt.text: Contraindicated; NSAIDs worsen acute kidney injury.

monitoring: Liver injury risk: maximum 15 days, second-line only. Liver function: stop permanently at any sign of liver injury or abnormal liver tests; avoid other hepatotoxic drugs and alcohol. Kidney function in CKD and heart failure; gastrointestinal bleeding (EMA 2004, 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Contraindicated under 12 years; adolescents 12 to 18 years as adults (EMA 2004).

renal.recommendation: Contraindicated under 12 years; adolescents follow adult kidney rules (contraindicated if CrCl <30).
